ant.antfact1: There are over 20,000 different kinds of ants. They can be found pretty much across our whole planet. Especially at picnics!
ant.antfact2: Ants can be found everywhere there is land except Antarctica. Which is a shame because "The Ants of Antarctica" sounds like a movie.
ant.antfact3: Bilbies don't drink water, but they get moisture from eating fruit, seeds, and insects, including ants – but they have to eat a lot of them!

bilby.bilbyfact1: Bilbies can rotate their enormous ears! This helps them listen for danger or hunt for small animals to eat.
bilby.bilbyfact2: Bilbies have terrible eyesight but a terrific sense of smell! This helps them to navigate at night.
bilby.bilbyfact3: Bilby mothers have a pouch like a kangaroo, but it opens backwards so that it doesn't fill with dirt when they're digging!
bilby.bilbyfact4: Bilbies don't need to drink water. They get the moisture they need from eating insects, fruit, seeds, and insect larvae.
bilby.bilbyfact5: Some Australians celebrate Easter by eating bilbies made out of chocolate. The money raised helps to protect the bilbies.
bilby.bilbyfact6: Bilbies are nocturnal – they come out at night to hunt for food!
bilby.bilbyfact7: Bilbies are great diggers, digging dozens of underground tunnels in the soft desert sand. They live there, protected from the hot sun.
bilby.bilbyfact8: Bilbies eat dirt when they're digging for food, like seeds and bulbs. They poop the dirt out!
bilby.bilbyfact9: Bilbies must be careful when they are above ground. Owls, dingoes, foxes, and eagles all like to eat bilbies.
bilby.bilbyfact10: Bilbies like to eat witchetty grubs, the juicy larvae from moths, which they can find buried in the sand.
bilby.bilbyfact11: Bilbies are omnivores, which means they eat both plants and animals. For bilbies, that includes seeds and insects.
bilby.bilbyfact12: Australia is a massive island. Some animals don't live anywhere else in the world, including bilbies, kangaroos, wombats, and koalas.

bulb.bulbfact1: Some flowers grow from bulbs not seeds. An onion is a kind of bulb. Bilbies love to eat these Australian bush onions!

dactyseed.dactyseedfact1: Bilbies find seeds to eat by digging in the soft sand. They like grass seeds, which often grow near water.

dingo.dingofact1: Dingoes are wild dogs and are related to wolves. They often live in old rabbit holes, especially if there's water nearby.
dingo.dingofact2: Dingoes are the biggest land predator in Australia. Sharks are bigger but they can't live in the Australian desert.
dingo.dingofact3: Dingoes hunt for bilbies and many other animals, small ones, like rats and mice, to big ones, like sheep and even kangaroos!
dingo.dingofact4: The red-brown fur of the dingo makes it hard to see in the red-brown dirt of the desert. This helps it to be a very sneaky hunter!
dingo.dingofact5: Dingoes talk to each other using almost 20 different sounds. They are mostly whining noises and howls – dingoes don't bark.

eagle.eaglefact1: Wedge-tailed eagles glide on the warm air above the desert and swoop down quickly to catch small animals like bilbies, rabbits, and rats.

fox.foxfact1: Foxes were brought to Australia by settlers many years ago. Now they are a pest to animals who have always lived there – including bilbies!

grasshopper.grasshopperfact1: There are about 3,000 different species of grasshopper in Australia. Bilbies will eat any of them if they don't hop away!

grub.grubfact1: Like caterpillars, witchetty grubs are larvae when they are little. They become moths – if they're not eaten by birds or bilbies!
grub.grubfact2: Some people in Australia eat witchetty grubs. If eaten raw, the grubs taste like almonds. When cooked, they taste like chicken!
grub.grubfact3: These grubs live about two feet underground. Most animals can't find them, but bilbies can because they like to dig.
grub.grubfact4: Bilbies eat witchetty grubs raw, but there are lots of ways to cook them. Raw, some say they taste like nuts; cooked, like fried eggs.

owl.owlfact1: Bilbies come out at night to hunt. But so do owls – and owls eat bilbies, if they can catch them!

termite.termitefact1: These insects are termites. In Australia, they are called white ants. They clear up waste by eating dead plants, leaves, and animal poop!

yakirraseed.yakirraseedfact1: These seeds grow into small spiky desert plants – if bilbies don’t eat them first!
